sections.heading: Four Things You Can Check Before You Call
body: Check what you safely can. Is the thermostat set to cool, with fresh batteries if it takes them? Is the breaker for the outdoor unit on? Is the air filter clogged? Is the outdoor fan turning?
If you see ice on the copper line or water around the indoor unit, switch the system off and call. Running a struggling air conditioner can turn a small repair into a bigger one.
The TSI office is open Monday to Friday, 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM. If the AC quits outside those hours, call anyway, because TSI offers after-hours emergency service.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong With a Central Air Conditioner
body: The house won't cool, the air from the vents is lukewarm, or the outdoor fan sits still while the unit hums. Most of those calls come back to one part, and finding which one is the first job.

items.title: A weak capacitor
items.text: The capacitor gives the fan motor and compressor the jolt they need to start. When it weakens, the unit hums and the fan won't spin.

items.title: A clogged filter or a dirty coil
items.text: Dust cuts airflow, and with too little airflow a coil can freeze over. Cleaning it is the fix, and the reason it clogged is worth knowing too.

items.title: Low refrigerant
items.text: An air conditioner doesn't use refrigerant up. If it's low, something is leaking, and topping it off without finding the leak only delays the next call.

items.title: A tired fan motor
items.text: A squeal, a rattle or a slow fan is an early warning. A motor replaced before it quits is usually a smaller job than one replaced after.

items.title: A failed compressor
items.text: This is the big one. On an older unit a compressor failure is often the moment repair and replacement need to be priced side by side.

sections.heading: Repair It or Replace It: A Rule You Can Check
body: If it's a capacitor, a motor or a dirty coil, repair is the answer, and it costs a fraction of a new system. If the unit is old, repairs keep stacking up, or the compressor has failed, that's the time to price a new one.
Ask for both numbers, the repair and the replacement, and put them next to each other. Sizing a new system is free, by quote and technician visit, so looking at replacement doesn't cost you anything.
Central air conditioners are among the incentives in the Ameren Illinois Energy Efficiency Program, and TSI is a registered Program Ally in it. Ask what applies to your job.

sections.heading: A Spring Cleaning Before the First Hot Week
body: TSI's advice is to have the system inspected twice a year, spring and fall, and to rotate the filter monthly. For the air conditioner, spring is the one that counts. A check before the heat catches a weak part on a mild day, when nobody is waiting on you.
The monthly filter rotation costs next to nothing and protects the coil from the dust problem described above.
